### Attribution, so the number is right by construction rather than by luck

The compiler moves every async body, iterator and lambda into a nested generated class, and the
SOURCE LINES go with it. Those entries are excluded by C2, so their lines are **attributed back
to the type that declares them** rather than discarded. Without this, a type whose async body
ran would read as ZERO, and a type whose async body never ran would be MISSED entirely — the
SP-118 shape exactly.

| | |
|---|---|
| excluded entries whose lines were attributed back to a shipped type | 724 |
| types with NO entry of their own — every source line lives in a state machine | 3 |
| of those, driven | 3 |
| of those, ZERO (would have been missed entirely without attribution) | 0 |

Measured on this tree, attribution changes the zero count by **nothing**: no type in the list
below has a generated child that executed (0 false zeros), and no undriven type exists only as
a state machine (0 missed zeros). It is kept because the next tree is not this tree.

## WHAT THIS CENSUS CANNOT SEE — read this before the number

**1. A type with no source-mapped IL never enters the universe at all — it is INVISIBLE, not
zero, and this is the largest thing the census cannot see.** The collector reports coverage by
SOURCE LINE, so a type only enters the report when it owns at least one IL instruction carrying
a sequence point. Measured from the shipped assembly's own TypeDef and MethodDef tables:

| | |
|---|---|
| type definitions in `CcpClient.Desktop.dll` | 1324 |
| of those, authored name shape (would survive C2/C3) | 884 |
| of those, reaching this census | 649 |
| **INVISIBLE rather than zero** | **235** |
| — no method body at all: interfaces without default members, enums, abstract-only | 212 |
|     interfaces 70, enums 62, structs 45, classes 35 | |
| — has a method body, but no source line maps to it | 23 |

The second category is the subtle one and it is worth naming precisely, because it is easy to
state wrongly. `OrphanSafePlayerFactory<TPlayer>.ConstructionSlot`
(`client/src/CcpClient.Desktop/Audio/AudioSeams.cs:228-233`) is a fields-only nested class, and
it does NOT lack IL — the compiler supplies it a default constructor. What it lacks is a
sequence point: no line of source maps to that constructor, so the collector emits nothing and
the type is absent. The rest of this category is Avalonia's XamlIl support surface
(`CompiledAvaloniaXaml.XamlIlHelpers`, `XamlDynamicSetters`, `!XamlLoader`, the per-file
`NamespaceInfo:/...` types), which is generated straight to IL from `.axaml` with no C# source
behind it.

**Those XamlIl types are why the UNCLASSIFIED valve below reads zero, and the reason is not the
one it looks like.** They exist in the shipped assembly, they carry IL, and their names would
pass every clause of the rule — but they never enter the report, so the valve never sees them.
An empty valve here means *nothing unexplained reached the report*, not *nothing unexplained
exists in the assembly*.

Nothing in this census speaks about any of those types. They are not dead and not alive here;
they are outside the instrument.

**2. A MEMBER-LESS RECORD READS ZERO EVEN WHEN A TEST CONSTRUCTS IT. Do not trust a
`construction-invisible` row without reading the code.** For `sealed record Exit : Base;` the
compiler emits no sequence point for the construction it synthesises, so the type's ONLY
line-mapped member is the copy constructor, which nothing calls. The type then reports one
instrumented line, zero covered — indistinguishable from genuinely dead.

This was MEASURED with a controlled probe rather than reasoned about: a member-less record and
an otherwise identical one-member record were constructed by the same passing fact; the
member-less one landed in the zero list and the one-member control did not. The live instance
is `DtrhProtocol.DtrhPageMessage.Exit`, which `DtrhProtocolTests.cs:24` parses from
`{"type":"exit"}` on a green theory row — and which this census still calls zero.

**13 of the 42 rows below carry this marker.** They are NOT
excluded, because excluding them would be widening a rule to shorten a list. They are marked,
because a census that cannot tell you which of its own rows are weak evidence is worse than one
that can. Treat a `construction-invisible` row as *unproven in both directions*.

**3. Executed is not tested.** A line executed incidentally — a constructor run to build a
fixture, a `ToString` in an assertion message — counts as executed here. This census can prove
a type is untouched. It can never prove one is verified.

**4. A dead HALF of a live partial class is invisible.** Coverage is unioned across a type's
entries, so a type is zero-execution only when no half ran. That is a method-level question and
this is a type-level census.

**5. The census is OS-CONDITIONED — but a platform predicate only excuses a zero when it selects
an OS this census did NOT run on.** Generated on `windows`. A row is marked from a
platform predicate in the type's own source file, with comments stripped so prose about a
predicate never marks anything, and **the mark records its polarity** — because a
direction-blind marker launders zeros in the reassuring direction, which is the one failure
this whole census exists to refuse.

| mark | count | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| `other-os-gated` | 4 | the file's code selects an OS this run was not on, so the MACHINE may explain the zero — check the other OS before believing the row |
| `same-os-code` | 12 | the file's code selects `windows`, the OS this run WAS on, so **the machine does not explain the zero at all** — the type would be MORE dead elsewhere, not less |

The distinction matters most on the largest dead surface below. A `same-os-code` row is not
excused by anything: its platform predicate is satisfied here and the code still never ran.
**A type is confidently dead only when both OS legs agree, and neither mark ever changes the
count.**

**6. Zero is a fact about the suite, not a verdict on the code.** A type may be exercised by a
headed capture, by the publish gate, or by nothing at all. The census names candidates; it does
not file defects.

## The shipped-type rule

The exclusion rule is BIGGER than the answer, so it is the risk. Every clause is defended in
one sentence and states what it removed. Widening a clause to shorten the list would be
`allowedSkips`-as-quarantine wearing a new hat.

Universe: **3958** `<class>` entries across every cobertura report.

| clause | what it removes | removed | defence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | any entry outside package `CcpClient.Desktop` | 1902 | The row asks about SHIPPED types, and CcpClient.Desktop is the assembly that gets published; CcpClient.Tests and CcpClient.HeadlessTests are not shipped, and an unexecuted test class is the floor's question (a test count), not this census's. |
| **C2** | any entry with a dot-segment matching `^<` | 728 | No C# identifier may begin with '<', so a dot-segment that does was emitted by the compiler and written by nobody: <>c, <>c__DisplayClassN_M, <Method>d__N, <<Method>b__N_M>d, <>c<TModel>, <Module>, <PrivateImplementationDetails>, and the [GeneratedRegex] tree including its nested RunnerFactory/Runner. |
| **C3** | any entry whose FINAL dot-segment matches `^XamlClosure_[0-9]+$` | 4 | Avalonia's XAML compiler emits these nested classes for deferred content and no source file declares them; they are the only compiler-generated shape in this assembly that does not begin with '<'. Anchored at both ends so a type someone actually named XamlClosure_Registry survives. |
| **kept** | merged by fully-qualified name into types | 1324 entries → 649 types | a partial class is ONE type; coverage is unioned |
| *(attribution)* | C2/C3 entries whose lines return to their declaring shipped type | 724 re-attributed, 0 dropped | the compiler moved those source lines out of the type; attribution moves them back |

### C1's counterfactual, measured rather than argued

C1 removes the unshipped test assemblies. Published so the clause is not taken on trust: of
**1891** authored-shape types in `CcpClient.Tests` and `CcpClient.HeadlessTests`,
**53** have zero executed lines. That number is a diagnostic about test-side
helpers and never enters the answer above.

### UNCLASSIFIED — the rule is incomplete (0)

An entry that survives C1-C3 but is not under CcpClient.Desktop.* was neither classified nor understood. It is NOT dropped: a future source generator inventing a new shape must appear as an unexplained row rather than silently joining the zero list or silently vanishing. Fail loud, never quiet.

None. Every entry surviving the clauses is under `CcpClient.Desktop.*`.
